Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: The applicant makes an Application to Reopen the claim for refugee protection.
The Refugee Protection Division (RPD) denies the Application to Reopen.

I have reviewed the applicant's request to reopen the claim for refugee protection, and upon reviewing all of the relevant factors, including Rule 62 and 63 of the Refugee Protection Division Rules1 (RPD Rules), as well as the relevant case law, the reasons for my decision follow. Background of RPD claim

A review of the Immigration and Refugee Board's (the Board) file indicates that the applicant (referred to as "the claimant" during the process of the claim) filed an inland claim for refugee protection on December 13, 2017 at in Etobicoke, Ontario. She was interviewed by an officer with the assistance of a Mandarin interpreter and her refugee claim was referred to the RPD on the same date. The applicant presented several forms, including a completed Basis of Claim (BOC), two schedules, and a declaration, along with a Use of a Representative form, indicating that she was represented by legal counsel who assisted her in preparing and initiating the claim. The applicant was informed by the referring officer that a hearing into her claim for refugee protection would be held on April 17, 2018; she was then provided with a Notice to Appear (NTA) at 74 Victoria Street, Toronto on that date.

The NTA specified that if the applicant failed to appear for the hearing as scheduled, she was required to attend a special hearing on April 24, 2018 to provide an explanation for her failure to appear, or her claim might be declared abandoned.

In a letter dated January 18, 2018 the RPD notified the applicant and her counsel that the hearing scheduled to take place on April 17, 2018 had been postponed for administrative reasons and a new date would be fixed as early as possible.

In a Notice to Appear dated May 4, 2018 the RPD notified the applicant and her counsel that a new date had been fixed and the hearing would be held on June 21, 2018. The NTA was transmitted by regular mail to the applicant's address at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, the same address on record since the claim was referred to the Board on December 13, 2017.

The NTA specified that if the applicant failed to appear for the hearing as scheduled, she was required to attend a special hearing on July 28, 2018 to provide an explanation for her failure to appear, or her claim might be declared abandoned. Applicant did not attend hearing on June 21, 2018

The applicant failed to appear at the hearing scheduled for June 21, 2018. Counsel attended and indicated that the applicant was ill. In view of the applicant's failure to appear on the date as scheduled, she was required to attend the special hearing on June 28, 2018, as per the NTA transmitted to her address, and provide an explanation for her absence.

On June 26, 2018 counsel faxed a copy of a medical note to the RPD. The note, dated June 20, 2018, is of a standard prescription format and contains the doctor's name and address, as well as the applicant's name. Rule 65 of the RPD Rules sets out the following: (5) If the claimant's explanation includes medical reasons, other than those related to their counsel, they must provide, together with the explanation, the original of a legible, recently dated medical certificate signed by a qualified medical practitioner whose name and address are printed or stamped on the certificate.

As per Rule 65 (6), the medical certificate must set out (a) the particulars of the medical condition, without specifying the diagnosis, that prevented the claimant from providing the completed Basis of Claim Form on the due date, appearing for the hearing of the claim, or otherwise pursuing their claim, as the case may be; and (b) the date on which the claimant is expected to be able to pursue their claim.

The medical note faxed to the RPD falls short of the above requirements, as it simply reads, "unable to work Jun 21, 22 2018 due to medical reason." Rule 65(7) indicates that if the medical certificate is not provided in accordance with sub-rules (5) and (6), the claimant must provide an explanation which must include (a) particulars of any efforts they made to obtain the required medical certificate, supported by corroborating evidence; (b) particulars of the medical reasons included in the explanation, supported by corroborating evidence; and (c) an explanation of how the medical condition prevented them from providing the completed Basis of Claim Form on the due date, appearing for the hearing of the claim or otherwise pursuing their claim, as the case may be.

I determine that the applicant submitted a medical certificate that was only marginally sufficient; furthermore, the applicant also did not attend the special hearing as required in order to explain her failure to appear on June 21, 2018. Applicant did not attend special hearing on June 28, 2018 to explain failure to appear

Counsel, who was present at the special hearing on June 28, 2018, did not present any additional information regarding the applicant's absence at the hearing, particulars of her medical condition, or reason for her failure to attend the special hearing and show cause why her claim should not be declared abandoned.

Given the applicant's failure to attend as required and failure to communicate with the Board, the presiding panel rendered its decision orally at the special hearing and, in accordance with section 168(1) of the Immigration Refugee Protection Act (IRPA),2 declared the claim abandoned on June 28, 2018.

On July 10, 2018, a Notice of Decision was sent to the applicant regarding the fact that her claim had been declared abandoned as a result of her failure to appear at the special hearing on June 28, 2018. Application to Reopen claim
On July 26, 2018, the Board received an Application to Reopen the applicant's refugee claim from a different counsel, who indicates that he has been retained to act on her behalf.

On August 1, 2018, new counsel of record provided a statutory declaration from the applicant, in which she states: "I did not attend the scheduled hearing on June 28, 2018 as I was not informed by the Refugee Protection Division of the date and my previous counsel ... did not inform me of the hearing date."
According to Rule 62(6) of the RPD Rules, the Division must not allow the application unless it is established that there was a failure to observe a principle of natural justice.
I find that there has been no failure to observe a principle of natural justice on the part of the Board and therefore this application must be denied.

The applicant states in her declaration that she was not informed-either by her previous counsel, or by the Board-of the special hearing date on June 28, 2018. I find this explanation unreasonable and contrary to the documents on file. As stated above, the applicant received notification from the Board that her hearing had been rescheduled for June 21, 2018, in the form of a Notice to Appear (NTA) sent to her mailing address on May 4, 2018.

There is no indication, such as returned mail on the file, that the applicant did not receive this NTA. In addition, the applicant was aware of the June 21, 2018 hearing date, as she provided the medical note indicating her absence on that date.

The NTA, which I conclude was indeed received by the applicant on a balance of probabilities, also clearly specified that if the applicant failed to appear for the hearing on June 21, 2018, she was required to attend a special hearing on July 28, 2018. At this special hearing, she would be afforded an opportunity to provide an explanation for her failure to appear, and to demonstrate that she was intent on proceeding with her claim for refugee protection in Canada.

I find that the applicant was represented by competent and experienced counsel throughout the proceedings of her refuge claim. Records show that previous counsel was in communication with the Board, attended both hearings as scheduled, faxed the rudimentary medical note to the Board when the applicant provided it to her, and attempted to contact the applicant regarding her failure to appear.

I find that the applicant's failure to appear at the hearing into her claim for protection without a reasonable explanation, and her failure to attend the special hearing as required in order to provide a reason why her claim should not be abandoned, have not been reasonably explained, and there has been no breach of a principle of natural justice. In this case, I find that the applicant's failure to act in a diligent manner does not justify the reopening of the claim.

For the foregoing reasons the request to reopen the claim of the applicant is denied. (signed) "M. Moc" M.
